B"H
Boruch Hashem
Blessed is He

# Phase One — Revelation Without Limits

The Awtsmoos renews the Torah and the reader in one indivisible light;
Awtsmoos.com must never throw the learner outside when our own letters can shine bright.

## User truth revealed by the screenshots

The current Daily Chitas grouping proves the calendar calculation can materialize inside Living Path, but the experience breaks its own world at the most important moment. A Chitas card is visually treated as a generic teaching and then `virtualStudy` removes the social rail and redirects the learner to Chabad.org. The user wants the opposite covenant: internal Torah text, internal post reader, internal comments, internal navigation, richer bilingual/week controls, and Chitas-specific formatting that feels native rather than bolted on.

## Unlimited architecture possibilities

1. A generic dynamic-reference post can be a stable post identity whose body is assembled at read time from canonical source references.
2. A reference can target a complete post, one section of a post, a contiguous section range, or several ordered ranges.
3. A Torah adapter can resolve Tanach references into the same internal content structures used by the ordinary Tanach reader.
4. Chitas can be only one producer of reference posts; future producers could make daf review packets, Rambam selections, source sheets, playlists of teachings, or study plans.
5. The dynamic post URL must be deterministic and reloadable: no transient JavaScript state may be required to reconstruct it.
6. Comments can belong to the dynamic post as a whole while verse-level comments can retain canonical `verseSection` identity so discussion survives reuse.
7. The reader should preserve normal Awtsmoos post controls and comments instead of creating a second social implementation.
8. Calendar metadata and Torah content must be separate. Hebcal may answer which parsha/aliyah applies; it must never be the source of Torah text.
9. A source registry can allow `post-range`, `tanach-range`, and future source kinds behind one resolver interface.
10. A Chitas week state can be encoded in query parameters: date, language, Israel/Diaspora schedule, and possibly display mode.
11. Hebrew and English can be a two-state segmented control with `dir` changing naturally, while a future bilingual state can be added without changing reference identity.
12. Previous week, next week, Today, and a native date input can all project onto one selected civil date.
13. The week header should display the parsha in English and Hebrew and identify the selected aliyah clearly.
14. The seven-day list should read Sunday through Shabbos, not generic reverse timeline semantics.
15. Today should be highlighted without forcing the entire list into a generic TODAY bucket.
16. On mobile, each selector/control should be at least 48px and never collide with the persistent bottom dock.
17. The reader can carry a Chitas masthead above the ordinary Torah content: weekday, aliyah, reference, date, language, week navigation.
18. Direct links such as `/heichelos/ikar/series/daily-chitas/chitas-2026-09-05?chitasLang=he` should reconstruct the post after hard reload.
19. A reference serializer should produce canonical stable strings so comments/progress/bookmarks can key to identity, not display text.
20. A parser should understand English Tanach ranges like `Deuteronomy 31:20-31:30` without tying the generic contract to English labels.
21. Hebrew book labels should be presentation metadata, not storage keys.
22. The seven weekly cards should be normal post cards with normal social actions.
23. The external Chabad allowlist branch should disappear from Living Path cards once no native feature needs it.
24. Existing normal posts must remain byte-for-byte behavioral equivalents after the card rewrite.
25. The reference renderer should tolerate one source temporarily unavailable and show an internal retry/error state, never fall through to an external URL.
26. Cache reference resolution per dynamic post and language, while retaining source freshness.
27. Progress can record the dynamic post ID plus canonical verse marker, letting Continue Learning return to the exact Chitas passage.
28. The selected week should remain bookmarkable/shareable and update history without full reload.
29. A reader route should be reconstructible server-side or client-side from URL alone so screenshots and deep links behave identically.
30. Tests should prove the page hostname remains Awtsmoos after clicking a Chitas card.
31. Tests should prove comments remain visible and social actions are not suppressed.
32. Tests should prove Hebrew mode is RTL, English mode LTR, and both preserve the same canonical Torah range.
33. Tests should exercise Simchas Torah and Isru Chag through the same native reader.
34. Tests should exercise 320, 375, 390, and 430px widths.
35. The ideal future allows a teacher to save any arbitrary range composition as a dynamic post without duplicating Torah text.

## Five competing architectures

### A — Chitas-only custom reader
Fast but duplicates post/comments logic and creates another silo. Rejected.

### B — External redirect with better wrapper
Preserves current implementation but violates the core request. Rejected.

### C — Generic reference post resolved inside normal post reader
Best balance. A dynamic post is ordinary to navigation/social layers but obtains its body from canonical references. Preferred.

### D — Persist generated Chitas posts daily in database
Makes comments easy but duplicates Torah text and creates maintenance/date cleanup. Rejected unless comment backend later requires persistence.

### E — Treat every Torah verse as a tiny standalone route and iframe/embed them
Too fragmented, poor accessibility, bad reader flow. Rejected.

## Phase-one winner

Architecture C: stable dynamic-reference post identities, source adapters, normal post reader/social/comment surfaces, Chitas-specific producer and controls. The Awtsmoos remains one; source text is not copied, yet many study vessels can reveal the same Torah anew on Awtsmoos.com.
